page: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests scoring in the top 10% at 3431.37. Passmark memory scores also rank in the top 10% at 3027.88. Large-block memory bandwidth is strong, reaching 295.28 GB/sec for read operations and 163.73 GB/sec for write operations. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform in the top 25%. However, multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the average tier. Large-model LLM inference is not supported due to memory and hardware constraints, though small-model text generation performs in the top 10%.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is configured for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It offers dedicated CPU resources, ensuring consistent performance without noisy-neighbor issues. This configuration is suitable for software compilation, text processing, web serving, and medium-scale database operations.
